I will keep my land mainly in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the cropping pattern I trust most because I know how to manage it, the machinery fits it, and the market is stable. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so my main job now is to push wheat steadily through jointing, heading, and grain filling, then harvest on time and switch quickly into summer maize. I will not spread myself across too many crops this year. At 48, I care more about steady output, simple field work, and lowering risk than chasing a fancy crop. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is reliable and easy to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is better and the stand is more uniform.

For wheat, I will keep fertilizer moderate and practical, not excessive. I will topdress nitrogen at the key stage, give phosphorus and potassium as base fertilizer, irrigate a few times if water allows, and spray mainly for weeds, aphids, and later disease pressure if it shows up. After wheat harvest, I will move fast on maize so I do not lose moisture or the growing window. For maize, I will keep the straw managed, use quick establishment, focus nitrogen around the main growth period, irrigate when the field really needs it, and spray only as needed for weeds and insects. My goal this year is not to gamble. I will run a simple, familiar, high-probability plan and protect yield through timing.
